note:
Round 3 of the crow's feet before/after set for the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Earlier rounds are kept; nothing is deleted.

MALCOLM, 2026-08-25 - THE CHANGE THAT DEFINES THIS ROUND. The previous rounds briefed an IDENTICAL camera position, IDENTICAL lighting and 'nothing differs between the panels except the skin'. That is why they read as retouched pairs rather than as evidence: a real clinical trial cannot pose someone identically weeks later, and a perfectly matched pair looks like one photograph edited twice. So this round asks for TWO SESSIONS, not two frames - the same woman photographed at two different clinic visits, weeks apart, with the same studio setup.

Naturally different between the visits, all of it SMALL: head angle by a few degrees, camera distance very slightly, gaze direction, the key light a little higher and a touch warmer or cooler, a few strands of hair, the background's brightness and gradient, the garment at the edge of frame, and her natural colour from one day to the next.

THE TWO HALVES OF THIS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE AND THE BRIEF STATES BOTH EXPLICITLY. Session variance is bounded: too much and the panels stop reading as the same woman at the same site, and the comparison stops being a comparison. So the identity anchors are held FIXED - same side of the face, same anatomical region filling the panel, and the permanent marks (moles, freckles, sun spots) in the same places on her skin. Those marks are what let a viewer verify it is one person; the hair, light and pose are what make it look like two visits.

INHERITED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE, WHICH SURVIVES THE CHANGE UNTOUCHED: the number and position of the creases is the same in both panels and NO CREASE MAY DISAPPEAR. Only depth and shadow change. Session variance applies to the photograph, never to the finding.
  * MAGNITUDE AS A FRACTION OF DEPTH so it is checkable rather than a matter of taste: f1 about half, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest but still plainly visible.
  * CAUCASIAN MIDDLE-AGED WOMEN, three visibly different individuals across the three blocks, so one woman never appears enrolled in three studies on one page.
  * NO LETTERING FROM ANY ENGINE. Every percentage is composited afterwards by scripts/label-before-after.py. MATRIXYL failed in ~30 of 50 candidates on this project and a correct PDRN was resampled into PORN; a garbled efficacy figure is a false clinical claim on a live storefront.
  * SKIN REALISM SPECIFIED POSITIVELY - pore size varying by zone, individual outsized pores, asymmetric freckling, capillary flush, matte-to-oily variation. And the words sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated stay banned: they render as speckled white highlights that read as dry flaking.
  * THE DIPTYCH. All 99 candidates of the previous rounds landed their seam within 0.8% of centre. Session variance will make the seam MORE visible, which is correct - these are two photographs butted together, not one continuous frame.

COLOUR: Acetyl's scene colour is Pearl grey D8D6D4, as the GROUND behind the skin, never a cast on it. CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  crow's feet, two sessions
slots.prompt:
Two separate unretouched clinical photographs of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at two different clinic visits, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. The left panel is the first visit, the right panel is the follow-up.

THESE ARE TWO SESSIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. A real trial cannot pose someone identically weeks later, and a pair that matches perfectly looks retouched. So everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a second visit would naturally change is slightly different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN AT THE SAME PLACE ON HER FACE: a tight macro of the outer corner of one eye and the temple beside it of the same side of her face fills both panels; her permanent marks - moles, freckles, sun spots - form the same pattern in the same places on her skin; the same iris colour, the same brow shape, the same character of lash line.

NATURALLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO VISITS, AND ALL OF IT SUBTLE: her head is turned a few degrees differently and the camera sits very slightly closer in one panel than the other, so the framing is not identical; her gaze goes in a slightly different direction; the key light sits a little higher and a touch warmer at the second visit, so the shadows fall a little differently and the highlight on her skin sits in a slightly different place; a few strands of hair lie differently and one loose strand crosses the frame in only one of the panels; the pale grey background is a slightly different brightness with its gradient falling a little differently; if any clothing shows at the edge of the frame it is a different garment, in a different colour, at a different height; and her natural colour is a little different from one day to the other.

NONE OF THESE DIFFERENCES IS LARGE. A viewer must never doubt that it is the same woman photographed at the same place on her face. Do not change the pose substantially, do not switch to the other side of the face, and do not change the character of the lighting.

She is a white European woman of about fifty-two, with fair skin, blue-grey eyes and light brown hair drawn back off her face. She wears no makeup at either visit. The framing is a tight macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE: the lower lid, the lash line, the outer corner, and the flat of the temple beside it, with the brow partly in frame at the top. No mouth, no nose, no hairline, no ear. The eye is open and relaxed at both visits, the expression neutral, not smiling and not squinting.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the creases is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles and freckles are all still there, in the same places on her skin. What has changed between the two visits is only HOW DEEP the creases are.

THE SKIN IS THE SUBJECT AND IT MUST BE REAL. Pores vary in size and in density across the frame - noticeably larger and more open toward the centre of the face, finer and tighter out at the edge - with two or three individual pores clearly larger than their neighbours. Sun-freckling is scattered and asymmetric, with one small raised brown mole. A faint diffuse capillary flush warms the skin. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light. The skin is slightly oily and light-catching in one area and completely matte in another. This is a documentary photograph of a real face, not a beauty campaign.

AT THE FIRST VISIT, in the LEFT panel, the outer corner of the eye is creased into a fan of four or five expression lines spreading across the temple, each folded deeply enough to hold a distinct shadow along its length, with a finer crepey network gathered beneath the lower lid.

AT THE FOLLOW-UP VISIT, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE CREASES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as deep as before - the fold softer, the shadow it holds much lighter, its edges less sharply defined. The deepest one is still plainly visible. Her moles and freckles are all still there in the same places on her skin.

At both visits a soft directional key from the upper left with a gentle fill rakes just enough across the surface to describe the relief of the skin. The background is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4, thrown softly out of focus. Shot on a 100mm macro lens, sharp, honest and completely unretouched.
